# Generated store queries with no production caller.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS SEPARATELY. Phase 20.1's reachability guard runs
# x/tools/cmd/deadcode, which by design does NOT report dead functions in
# GENERATED files. internal/store/gen is generated, so the entire store
# layer was a blind spot — and that is exactly where B42 hid: nothing in
# production ever called UpsertSyncSubscription, so no entity was ever
# subscribed to any route and the whole ESI sync engine had nothing to do.
#
# Same contract as allowlist.txt: a new uncalled query fails the guard, and
# so does an entry here that has gained a caller. This file should SHRINK.

# B42 — CLOSED in Phase 20.1.1: UpsertSyncSubscription now has a production
# caller and has been removed from this group. What remains are subscription
# MANAGEMENT surfaces that still have none — an operator cannot snooze,
# disable, or opt a subscription out of caching except by SQL, and nothing
# surfaces recent sync runs. Reconciliation sets `enabled` through
# DisableUnscopedSubscriptions, which is why SetSyncSubscriptionEnabled is
# still unused.
#
# PHASE 20.2: SnoozeSyncSubscription left this group. §5.5 requires a 429 —
# and every deliberate gateway refusal — to snooze the affected subscription
# rather than fail its job, and internal/sync/worker/unavailable.go is now
# that caller. The column had existed since Phase 6 and nothing had ever
# written to it.
ListRecentSyncRuns
SetSyncNoCacheOptIn
SetSyncSubscriptionEnabled

# B24 — CLOSED in Phase 20.5. CreateWebhookEndpoint and
# ListWebhookEndpointsForUser have production callers (internal/api/v1/
# webhooks.go), and RevokeWebhookEndpoint was DELETED rather than kept:
# RevokeWebhookEndpointForOwner supersedes it by putting ownership in the
# predicate instead of in a Go-side check somebody can omit. Closing a defect
# by adding a caller for the weaker of two queries would have been the
# allowlist wagging the codebase.

# B26 — CLOSED in Phase 20.2 apart from one reader. GetRole, ListPermissions,
# ListEffectivePermissions and SetUserActive all gained production callers
# with the role-management surface (internal/api/v1/admin_roles.go) and the
# PATCH /admin/users/{id} fix. What is left is the one query with no natural
# consumer: nothing in HANGAR looks a user up BY their main character, and
# inventing an endpoint to give it one would be the allowlist wagging the
# codebase.
GetUserByMainCharacterID

# B25 — alert routing, channels and the unknown-type boards
CountAlertTypesByDomain
CreateAlertRoutingRule
GetAlertType
ListAlertChannels
ListAlertEventsForCoalesceKeySince
ListAlertTypes
ListRecentAlertEvents
ListUnparseableCharacterNotifications

# B30 — CLOSED in Phase 20.5 for the WRITERS; these five are READERS, and
# each is waiting for an endpoint rather than for a dispatch entry. The
# distinction is the whole point of the defect: the writers now run (every
# fan-out route is subscribable, worker/syncset.go), so these tables are
# populated for the first time — and nothing serves them yet.
#
# ListCorporationProjectContributions in particular now has data to return:
# the contributors sync writes app.corporation_project_contribution with
# `contributed` as the amount (B38's leftover, closed in the same phase), and
# 20.7 added a second writer for it — the per-character contribution route.
GetCalendarEventDetail
GetPlanetColonyDetail
GetStarbaseDetail
ListCorporationProjectContributions

# B35 — TeamSpeak identity linking

# Platform and entitlement configuration has no surface
CreatePlatform
CreatePlatformGroup
ListEntitlementRulesForGroup
ListEntitlementRulesForSource
SetEntitlementRuleEnabled

# Open-vocabulary boards (Gate 6 surfaces these; no reader is wired)
AcknowledgeOpenVocabularyValue
CountUnacknowledgedOpenVocabulary
GetEsiScope
ListUnacknowledgedOpenVocabulary

# Housekeeping. THE THREE DELETES LEFT THIS GROUP IN PHASE 21 (defect B-2):
# DeleteExpiredSessions, DeleteExpiredEsiCacheEntries and DeleteStaleReplicas
# are called by internal/housekeeping.Sweeper, which `serve` runs on a timer.
# Until then none of the three had a production caller and no installation had
# ever deleted an expired session row — personal data (ip_address, user_agent,
# pkce_verifier) retained indefinitely.
#
# The heading this group used to carry — "rows accumulate forever" — was also
# WRONG about one of its members, and the correction is worth keeping because
# it changes what the remaining entry means. app.esi_cache_entry is bounded in
# practice: UpsertEsiCacheEntry is keyed on cache_key and overwrites, so the
# table tracks the number of distinct cache keys in flight (380 rows, 0
# expired, when the pre-v1.0 audit measured it) rather than growing without
# limit. The sweep reclaims the tail of keys nobody asks for any more.
#
# What is left here is not housekeeping that never runs; it is two queries
# with no caller for two different reasons:
#
# CountEsiCacheEntries — operational visibility with no surface to show it on.
#   It belongs to the admin-observability gap (N-4), not to retention: the
#   sweeper deliberately does not call it, because a count(*) per tick would
#   scan the table to produce a number nothing reads.
# DeregisterReplica — graceful deregistration at shutdown, never wired. The
#   heartbeat's own comment records why it is tolerable
#   (internal/telemetry/replica.go): a replica that exits without deregistering
#   ages out of the liveness window anyway, so this would only make a dead row
#   disappear sooner than the retention sweep removes it.
CountEsiCacheEntries
DeregisterReplica

# Domain readers awaiting the endpoint or screen that uses them.
# GetLatestSdeImport LEFT this group in Phase 20.5: `hangar admin sde-status`,
# `hangar admin import-sde --if-changed` and the boot-time SDE report all read
# it (B22).
# ListMailRecipients LEFT it in Phase 20.10: the /api/v2 shim's character.mail
# route renders each recipient as a legacy entity object, so the query finally
# has the caller it was written for. Worth noting WHICH surface closed it —
# /api/v1's mail endpoints still do not read recipients, so the compatibility
# shim is currently the only thing that exposes them, and a future /api/v1 mail
# detail screen is still owed.
CreateCharacterNote
CreateSquadApplication
GetAsset
GetContract
GetKillmail
GetMoonReport
GetShareLink
GetSquad
GetWalletBalance
ListAssetsByRootLocation
ListInvalidCharacterTokens
ListKillmailAttackers
ListKillmailItems
RecordApiTokenAccess

# Writers with no production caller. PHASE 20.7 (B48) emptied most of this
# block by wiring the handlers — fittings, killmails, insurance prices and
# contact notifications all have callers now and were removed here in the
# same commit that wired them.
#
# PHASE 20.8 removed the last two capability entries the same way.
# UpsertAlliance and UpsertLocation were listed here because capabilities #37
# and #41 "need machinery that does not exist (an alliance-scoped
# acting-character elector; a location-id enumeration query)". Both were
# built: internal/sync/worker/alliance.go with the EntityAlliance branch of
# internal/sync/election.go, and db/queries/reference.sql's
# ListUnresolvedStationIDs / ListCharacterStructureIDs. THIS SUITE IS WHAT
# FORCED THE ENTRIES OUT — it fails on an allowlist entry that has gained a
# caller, in the same way it fails on a caller-less query, so the file cannot
# quietly outlive the reason it was written.
#
# What is left is left for reasons that are not capability gaps:
#
#   UpsertCharacterIntelEdge — the intel graph writes its edges through a
#   different statement; see the intel block below.
#
#   UpsertReplicaHeartbeat — a deliberate keep: internal/telemetry/replica.go
#   issues its own statement because it must first probe to_regclass, so the
#   generated twin has never been used.
UpsertCharacterIntelEdge
UpsertReplicaHeartbeat

# B45 — reads app.corporation_role, which has NO production writer anywhere
# and is therefore permanently empty. Phase 20.1.1 moved the acting-character
# elector off it onto app.character_role, which is where ESI's
# GET /characters/{character_id}/roles actually lands. This query is kept
# because /corporations/{id}/roles is a real ESI route HANGAR syncs into that
# table via SyncCorporationRoles — the reader has simply never had a
# legitimate consumer. Its remaining caller is the admin surface that does
# not exist yet.
ListCorporationRoles

# ── PHASE 20.6: THREE QUERIES THIS GUARD HAD BEEN FALSELY PASSING ────────
# Until 20.6 the caller scan read RAW FILE BYTES, so a query named in a
# COMMENT counted as a production caller. generated_test.go now tokenises and
# keeps only identifiers, and these three fell out the moment it did: each
# appears in the tree exactly once, in prose.
#
# UpsertSyncSubscription is the one that matters. It is defect B42's OWN
# query — "nothing in production ever called UpsertSyncSubscription" — and
# the comment in internal/sync/subscribe/reconcile.go that documents B42 was
# the only thing making it look called. B42 was closed by wiring the three
# Reconcile*Subscriptions queries, not this one; the generated twin has never
# had a caller, and the guard built to catch precisely that was hiding it
# behind the sentence explaining it.
CheckPermission
ListPendingProvisioningAudit
UpsertSyncSubscription
